html:
The Rikbaktsa are an Indigenous people of northern Mato Grosso in Brazil, living along the Juruena, Arinos and Sangue rivers. Their language is usually placed in the large Macro-Gê family.

Settlers called them the canoe people for their skill on the rivers, and "wooden ears" for the plugs they wore in their earlobes. They fought off rubber tappers of the rubber boom era for decades. Jesuit missionaries made peaceful contact in the late 1950s and early 1960s, but epidemics then killed most of the people. Their neighbours include the Apiaká, the Enawenê-nawê and the Cinta Larga.
